record_identity.title: AI-generated immigration-attorney impersonation reportedly defrauded Bronx resident of $4,820

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Angel Leal AI impersonation scam against Victor Hernandez
incident_identity.date_basis: AIID records 19 August 2026 as the incident date; ABC7 reported the victim's account on 19–20 August 2026. The precise dates of each payment and document transfer are not independently established.

summary: A Bronx legal resident reported losing $4,820 and providing Social Security and residency documents after responding to an AI-generated social-media advertisement impersonating Miami immigration attorney Angel Leal. Leal said he had no involvement and that his identity had been cloned across thousands of fake profile videos.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: ABC7 directly interviewed Victor Hernandez and Angel Leal. Hernandez reported sending $4,820 through Zelle, providing Social Security and residency documents, falling behind on rent and electricity, and receiving further demands for money. Leal stated that the advertisement was based on his identity without permission and that thousands of fake profile videos using his likeness had been taken down. WLRN separately reported a broader pattern of AI-generated impersonation scams using Leal's identity. AIID indexes the bounded occurrence as Incident 1660.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Human scammers used AI-generated advertising impersonating attorney Angel Leal to create a false professional relationship and economic service premise, inducing payment and sensitive-document disclosure. The requester-side use of Leal’s identifiable likeness lacked his authorization; this supports the identity-authority failure without identifying an internal generator control. The AI system’s independent tactic-selection objective remains unproved. Requester-side identity-bound cloning without the attorney’s authorization supports the neutral likeness-authority failure; identifying the generator is not mandatory. This is separate from the payment/disclosure and social-engineering failures and the still-ambiguous AI-side objective. Static advertisements and human-directed follow-up do not establish an autonomous interactive participant. The independent dignity and autonomy assessment is Not aligned for the reported impersonation. Generator-specific controls are not established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence is relevant to identity-representation authority, synthetic-media provenance, deception-resistant decision pathways, payment and document-disclosure verification, and safeguards for high-vulnerability service contexts.
assessment_boundaries: No synthetic-media vendor, model or architecture is established by the reviewed evidence.
The record does not infer that a social-media platform created the synthetic content or knowingly participated in the fraud.
The wider number of victims and aggregate losses attributed to the broader Leal impersonation campaign are not treated as part of this bounded occurrence.
Law-enforcement reports are described in journalism but no investigative finding or prosecution is treated as established.
